checks_run.procedure: Run --historical for DG5 to DG1, --pipeline and --register DG6. Check DG6 in stages.json for any other inconsistency: state against its last history entry, monotone timestamps, legal transitions, candidate, manifest and round entries.
checks_run.command: for s in DG5 DG4 DG3 DG2 DG1; do node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage $s; done; node tools/gates/validate.mjs --pipeline; node tools/gates/validate.mjs --register DG6; python3 consistency script (stages-consistency.log)
checks_run.environment: Repository; Node 24.21.0. First pass at 3c07fa84e (14:44Z). Final pass at HEAD c9eca6539.
checks_run.expected: All exit 0. The DG6 history is legal and consistent.
checks_run.actual: Disclosed failure in the first pass. At 3c07fa84e, --historical DG5, DG4 and DG3 exited 1 on 'stages.json: DG6 state FIXING differs from last history entry REVIEWING' (run1-*.log). Commit 3c07fa84e had set the DG6 state to FIXING while appending the history entries FIXING 14:42:55Z and REVIEWING 14:42:56Z. The orchestrator corrected it at 14:45-14:46Z in c9eca6539 (state REVIEWING, 1 line), during my run. The DG2 and DG1 runs, which happened after that write, passed. Final pass at c9eca6539: DG5, DG4, DG3, DG2 and DG1 each print 'PASS gate DGn (historical)'; --pipeline prints 'PASS pipeline (active stage: DG6 REVIEWING)'; --register DG6 prints 'PASS register rules at DG6'; all exit 0. Consistency: state REVIEWING equals the last entry; timestamps are monotone; the transitions VERIFYING -> FIXING (06:42:33Z, with a note that it was recorded late) -> REVIEWING -> FIXING -> REVIEWING are legal. The candidate and manifest agree on 5e819f7a. The round-6 entry names domain and qa only, because code-security's round-5 PASS binds on this same candidate. gates/DG6.json still records the round-4 BLOCKED decision for 32e41b55. I do not raise the 3c07fa84e mismatch as a finding: it was committed fixed before my verdict, it is outside the candidate, and the binding validations pass at HEAD.

The register's disclosed limits I accept: the S15-014 not-found/not-demo states, LOAD-T20's dataset gap (D-199 item 2), and the REQ-S20-029/030 targets labelled provisional, not Mobily capacity. checks_run.procedure: Judge D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name) and the D-228 (4) out-of-scope ruling on cross-organization ids. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that names a sensitive record, or a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal. Read the worker's notification channel code (apps/worker/src/handlers/notifications.ts) and run the access suites.
checks_run.expected: No reader learns a hidden id or text that they could not already read.
checks_run.actual: Not a defect. At send time the channel fan-out checks restrictedForRecipient against the target, the work item's subject and the link. A restricted message carries the inbox.restricted key, no message parameters, and a link to the transformation home only (notifications.ts:598-612), so email or messaging names nothing. z13/z13b/z13c (served keys and error texts), z15 (version-bound restricted tokens across edits, grant changes and concurrent saves), z12b and the sensitive-reference inventory pass, so no token sequence loses or misplaces a hidden literal. D-229: a mapping or credential name can name an id only if an administrator who already sees that configuration types it; I accept it. D-228 (4): every helper checks the reader's own organizations; I accept it. My judgement is unchanged from rounds 3 and 5.

checks_run.procedure: Judge D-194 to D-196, D-199 item 2, D-202, D-203 to D-205 and D-239 against the master prompt's automation clauses (REQ-S12-019, REQ-S20-013) and the playbook.
checks_run.expected: Each decision is accepted, or a finding is raised.
checks_run.actual: All accepted. D-203: the batch and concurrency are bounded (defaults 8/4), with no action on events before enablement. D-204: a late event is evaluated against the version in force and enabled at its occurrence, from the 0122/0123 ledger; the version-at-occurrence suite passes. D-205: disabling a rule stops its pending events. The residual commit-order race documented in ADR-0043 is bounded: the action key is idempotent, a duplicate yields 'already', and an automation never decides a G1-G6 business approval. It is acceptable as documented. D-194 to D-196, D-199 item 2 and D-202 are unchanged from my earlier rounds. D-239: the five append-only audit_event.reason texts carry task and decision ids, not gate names, and are served by no reader route. Keeping them as history preserves the append-only audit, so I accept it.
